nodes.title: Matrix Types & Standard Operations
points: Order of matrix: m × n (m rows, n columns). A square matrix has m = n.
Diagonal matrix: Non-diagonal elements are 0 (a_ij = 0 for i ≠ j).
Scalar matrix: Diagonal matrix with all diagonal elements equal. Identity matrix I: diagonal elements are all 1.
Symmetric matrix: A^T = A (a_ij = a_ji). Skew-symmetric: A^T = −A (a_ij = −a_ji, diagonal elements a_ii = 0).
Every square matrix A can be uniquely expressed as sum of symmetric and skew-symmetric matrices: A = ½(A + A^T) + ½(A − A^T).
Matrix Multiplication: A_(m×n) × B_(n×p) = C_(m×p). Non-commutative in general: AB ≠ BA.

nodes.title: Minors, Co-factors & Adjoint Matrix
points: Minor (M_ij): Determinant of the sub-matrix obtained by deleting i-th row and j-th column of A.
Co-factor (A_ij): A_ij = (−1)^(i+j) M_ij. Co-factor matrix is [A_ij].
Adjoint Matrix (adj A): Transpose of the matrix of co-factors: adj A = [A_ij]^T.
Fundamental Adjoint Identity: A · (adj A) = (adj A) · A = |A| · I.
Determinant expansion using co-factors: a_i1 A_i1 + a_i2 A_i2 + a_i3 A_i3 = |A|; expansion along elements of a different row is ZERO.

nodes.title: Inverse of a Matrix & Existence
points: Definition: If A and B are square matrices of same order such that AB = BA = I, then B is the inverse of A, denoted A⁻¹.
Condition for existence: Matrix A must be NON-SINGULAR (|A| ≠ 0). If |A| = 0, A is singular and A⁻¹ does NOT exist.
Formula for Inverse: A⁻¹ = (1 / |A|) · adj A.
Uniqueness: If the inverse of a matrix exists, it is unique.

nodes.title: 2 × 2 Matrix Inverse Shortcut
points: For a 2 × 2 matrix A = [[a, b], [c, d]]:
Determinant: |A| = ad − bc.
Adjoint Shortcut: Swap the main diagonal elements (a ↔ d), and change the signs of off-diagonal elements (b → −b, c → −c): adj A = [[d, −b], [−c, a]].
Inverse: A⁻¹ = (1 / (ad − bc)) · [[d, −b], [−c, a]].
Calculation takes less than 5 seconds and avoids computing individual co-factors.

nodes.title: Elementary Transformations (Row & Column)
points: Three types of elementary row/column transformations: (1) Interchanging any two rows/columns (R_i ↔ R_j); (2) Multiplying elements of a row by non-zero scalar (R_i → k R_i); (3) Adding k times elements of one row to another (R_i → R_i + k R_j).
Finding A⁻¹ by Elementary Row Transformations: Start with A = I A. Apply identical row operations to LHS (reducing A to I) and RHS (converting I to A⁻¹), obtaining I = A⁻¹ A.
Finding A⁻¹ by Column Transformations: Start with A = A I. Apply column operations to get I = A A⁻¹.
If during row/column transformations a full row/column becomes all zeros, then A⁻¹ does not exist (|A| = 0).

formulas.label: Row transformation setup
formulas.expr: A = I A ⟶ I = A⁻¹ A

formulas.label: Column transformation setup
formulas.expr: A = A I ⟶ I = A A⁻¹

nodes.title: Properties of Inverse & Adjoint
points: Reversal Law: (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹ A⁻¹; (ABC)⁻¹ = C⁻¹ B⁻¹ A⁻¹.
Transpose & Inverse: (A^T)⁻¹ = (A⁻¹)^T.
Double Inverse: (A⁻¹)⁻¹ = A.
Determinant of Inverse: |A⁻¹| = 1 / |A|.
Adjoint of Product: adj(AB) = (adj B) · (adj A).
Determinant of Adjoint: |adj A| = |A|^(n − 1), where n is order of matrix.
Double Adjoint Determinant: |adj(adj A)| = |A|^((n − 1)²).
Double Adjoint Formula: adj(adj A) = |A|^(n − 2) · A.

nodes.title: System of Linear Equations: Inversion Method
points: System of linear equations: a₁x + b₁y + c₁z = d₁; a₂x + b₂y + c₂z = d₂; a₃x + b₃y + c₃z = d₃.
Matrix representation: A X = B, where A is 3×3 coefficient matrix, X = [x, y, z]^T, B = [d₁, d₂, d₃]^T.
Condition: Coefficient matrix A must be non-singular (|A| ≠ 0).
Solution: Pre-multiply by A⁻¹ ⟹ A⁻¹(AX) = A⁻¹B ⟹ X = A⁻¹ B.
Substitute A⁻¹ = (1/|A|) adj A and multiply with column matrix B to get unique values for x, y, z.

nodes.title: System of Linear Equations: Reduction Method
points: Write matrix equation A X = B.
Apply elementary row transformations to coefficient matrix A to convert it into an UPPER TRIANGULAR matrix (or lower triangular matrix), applying identical operations to B.
Target form: [[a₁₁, a₁₂, a₁₃], [0, a₂₂', a₂₃'], [0, 0, a₃₃']] · [x, y, z]^T = [d₁', d₂', d₃']^T.
Perform back-substitution: Solve bottom equation for z, substitute into 2nd row for y, and finally into 1st row for x.
Advantage: Involves fewer arithmetic calculations and no co-factor computation compared to the inversion method.

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Proofs & Matrix Inversion
points: Board Favourite #1: Prove that the inverse of a matrix, if it exists, is unique.
Board Favourite #2: Prove the reversal law of inverse: (AB)⁻¹ = B⁻¹ A⁻¹.
Board Favourite #3: Find inverse of a 3×3 matrix using Elementary Row Transformations (systematically create 1 at a₁₁, then 0s below; 1 at a₂₂, then 0s; 1 at a₃₃, then 0s above).
Board Favourite #4: Solve 3 linear equations using the Method of Inversion and Method of Reduction (4 marks each).
Board Presentation Tip: Always compute |A| FIRST. If |A| = 0, state immediately that A⁻¹ does not exist.

formulas.label: Uniqueness proof
formulas.expr: If AB = I and AC = I ⟹ B = C

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Determinant Hacks & Cayley-Hamilton
points: Scalar Factor Determinant: |k A| = kⁿ |A| for an n × n matrix (for 3×3, |2A| = 2³ |A| = 8 |A|).
Adjoint Determinant Shortcut: For 3×3 matrix, |adj A| = |A|²; |adj(adj A)| = |A|⁴.
Polynomial Equation Inverse Hack: If A satisfies A² − 5A + 7I = O, multiply by A⁻¹ ⟹ A − 5I + 7A⁻¹ = O ⟹ A⁻¹ = (1/7)(5I − A).
Diagonal Matrix Inverse: Inverse of diag(a, b, c) is simply diag(1/a, 1/b, 1/c).
Orthogonal Matrix: A A^T = I ⟹ A⁻¹ = A^T and |A| = ±1.
Trace of Matrix: tr(A) = sum of principal diagonal elements. tr(A + B) = tr(A) + tr(B); tr(AB) = tr(BA).

formulas.label: Matrix polynomial A⁻¹
formulas.expr: A² + pA + qI = O ⟹ A⁻¹ = −(A + pI) / q
